Writer

Writing · defined at writer.mbt:11

pub(all) struct Writer {
  buf : @buffer.Buffer
  config : Config
  refs : Map[Int32, Int32]
  mut next_ref : Int32
  mut fresh : Int32
}

Where a value goes: a buffer, the configuration it is written under, and the table of what has already been sent.

Everything the specification fixes is a method here, so that a type this package has never heard of can be written with the same primitives its own types are written with. Nothing here is private to a codec.

Fields

FieldMeaning
buf : @buffer.Buffer

The bytes so far.

config : Config

What this message is written under.

refs : Map[Int32, Int32]

The caller's key for a shared value, and the reference id it was given.

MoonBit has no identity to infer sharing from, so the key is the caller's: two writes of the same key send the value once and point at it after.

mut next_ref : Int32

The next reference id.

mut fresh : Int32

The key handed to the next value that takes a reference id without being given one: a tracked value the caller did not name still has to occupy its place in the id order, and the key it is filed under descends from -2, below root_key.

write_fresh

fn Writer::write_fresh(Self) -> Unit

The flag for a value that is tracked but was never named: it takes the next reference id, under a key of this writer's own below every caller's, so that the ids of the references that do name something still line up with a peer's.

write_head

fn Writer::write_head(Self) -> Unit

The header byte: the cross-language flag in bit 0.

The specification leaves bit 1 for out-of-band data and asks that it be 0 when there is none, which is always here: this package writes no out-of-band buffer.

write_ref

fn Writer::write_ref(Self, Int32) -> Bool

The flag for a reference to a value that has already been written, and whether it was: a key that names nothing yet writes nothing and answers false, because a reference to a value that is not on the wire cannot be written as one.

write_string

fn Writer::write_string(Self, String) -> Unit

A string: the header, then the bytes.

The encoding chosen is UTF-8, which the specification allows every language to read; LATIN1 and UTF-16 are read but not written, because a MoonBit string is Unicode and narrowing it would lose what is not in the other one.

write_tagged_i64

fn Writer::write_tagged_i64(Self, Int64) -> Unit

A sixty-four-bit signed integer that is usually small: four bytes carrying v << 1, or 1 and then eight bytes when it does not fit.

The low bit of the first four bytes is the tag, which is why the range that fits is [-2^30, 2^30-1] and not the whole of the thirty-two bits.

write_tagged_u64

fn Writer::write_tagged_u64(Self, UInt64) -> Unit

A sixty-four-bit unsigned integer that is usually small: four bytes carrying v << 1, or 1 and then eight bytes when it does not fit.

write_tracked

fn Writer::write_tracked(Self, Int32) -> Bool

The envelope of a value that may be written more than once, and whether the body still has to be written.

key is the caller's name for the value. The first time it is met, 0x00 goes out and the answer is true; after that, 0xFE and the reference id go out and the answer is false, because the value is already on the wire.

write_var_u36

fn Writer::write_var_u36(Self, UInt64) -> Unit

The string header: size << 2 | encoding, written as one byte while it fits in seven bits and as a varint when it does not.

Sizes under thirty-two bytes are most strings, so the single byte is the case worth having.
